Short Term Modeling Assumptions
The worst case limited mixing situation was assumed to occur with a 2 meters per second wind and an inversion height 600 m above the plant (510 meters above the surrounding terrain). Stability below the inversion was of Pasquill Class "C". Limited mixing conditions were assumed to last a maximum of five hours.
Inversion break-up maximum concentrations were calculated assuming F stability, a wind speed of 2 meters per second, and an inversion break-up interval t as defined by Pooler (1965) of 80 minutes. Because the two plant stacks reach two different effective stack heights, the two will "break" at different times and therefore calculations were done using only the Boiler stack parameters, those that will cause the higher ground level concentrations. Terrain was also considered in this calculation. Inversion break-up was assumed to last 45 minutes of the time interval average considered.
Fanning was calculated under F stability and 2 meters per second wind speed. It was assumed that there was direct impaction upon the terrain so that surface concentrations were equal to plume centerline concentrations averaged over 3 hours. It is highly unlikely that impactions will occur at one location 16 kilometers from the source for 3 hours because of the propensity of the narrow plume to wander at low wind speeds, however the concentrations were calculated assuming impaction lasting 3 hours at one location.
